title: SAVAGE PUSH DAY (Hypertrophy Log #3)
summary: Hypertrophy log of an upper/push day on his 'gentleman split': two giant sets of four exercises each, done 3-4 rounds, covering chest, long-head triceps, upper back, forearms and abs. He explains each movement with an eye on joint-friendly choices, because of his elbow tendinitis and scoliosis.
claims: The gentleman split is an upper/lower template where each upper day is free to emphasise different muscles, and he hits any fresh muscle even if it isn't a push movement
Forearms recover quickly and can be trained hard several times a week once you have built the work capacity; train them like a maniac for meaty forearms
Session structure: eight movements in two giant sets with no rest between exercises, resting only at the end of each round, for 3-4 rounds
He does only 8-12 sets of chest a week because chest is a strong point
Anyone doing dumbbell flies should try the power fly instead; biomechanically it makes more sense and you probably won't go back
Regular skull crushers wreck his elbow tendons; doing them with shoulder extension, closer to a lying triceps extension, avoids that
His scoliosis makes his arms drift to one side on extensions, but it has caused no problems
He defines failure as mechanical failure: stop the set the moment you need body English or a torso shift to finish a rep
Elbow tendinitis from push days is almost inevitable for lifters, so favour pressing variations that spare the elbows, such as slow negatives
On every push day include an upper-back and rear-shoulder movement to keep the shoulder blades mobile; shoulder problems often come from a weak, stiff upper back
Natural bodybuilding is about health: keep your joints healthy so you can still bench and overhead press in your 30s and 40s
Isolation movements like the reverse curl must be taken to failure
His shoulders were already fried that day, so he skipped vertical presses and trained chest and forearms instead
exercises: Power fly (barrel press)
neutral-grip dumbbell press with elbows flared to open the chest, more distance between chest and dumbbell, pause at bottom, slow negative
a hybrid of press and fly: the stability of pressing plus a deep stretch with less weight; triceps and shoulders don't limit it; easy on tendinitis
Cable pullover
before pull-ups
gets the shoulder blades moving and warms the lats without hurting pull-up performance
EZ-bar skull crusher with shoulder extension
feet on bench to lift the ribcage, upper back fully on bench, range that hits the long head
long-head triceps; easier on the elbows than standard skull crushers
Banded hammer curl
supinate at the bottom for a biceps stretch, pronate on the way up; to failure
biceps and forearms; prepares for pronated pull-ups and reverse curls
Sphinx triceps push-up
hands close, start by breaking at the elbows, slow negative
chest and long-head triceps for advanced lifters; easy on the tendons
Snow angels with a small plate
upper-back mobility work
keeps shoulders healthy by working the upper back and rear shoulder
Towel pull-up
close pronated grip on towels, slow negative, full stretch, explode up
humbling grip demand; good hypertrophy for forearms and upper back
Banded sit-up
band anchored at top of rack, slightly tilted to one side, slow negative, explosive up
avoids hip flexor involvement and lumbar extension that hurt backs; the tilt adds obliques and serratus; done fast the band does the work
Reverse curl (EZ bar)
false (thumbless) grip, close grip for full range, thumbs pointing up, squeeze at top
thumbless grip stops the wrist taking over; wide grip cuts range of motion
